_comment: Single source of truth for the location inner pages, the way
shared/segments.json is for the paid segment pages. Two registries, not
one, because they answer different questions: segments.json fixes six
HubSpot routing strings that never change, this file lists the places the
client has picked.
SCOPE SET 21 Aug 2026: one template, three pages. Adelaide, Perth and
Melbourne. The template is derived from the live Brisbane page, which the
design lead supplied as the reference because it performs. Its anatomy and
its gaps are recorded in locations/REFERENCE.md.
URL pattern is the client's existing one, /location/<slug>, so these pages
are siblings of a page that already ranks rather than new competitors for
the homepage. The slug is the URL segment and the folder name, and the two
never differ.
'readiness' is what the page can honestly carry today, not a build status.
It is separate from status on purpose: a page can be unblocked to build and
still be unable to fill a slot. Perth is the case that forced the split.
DECISIONS THAT SPAN BOTH PAGE FAMILIES LIVE IN segments.json, not here.
The CSS layer split of 21 Aug 2026 is recorded there under
openDecisions.cssLayerSplit. This file only carries decisions that affect
the location pages alone.

locations.label: Melbourne
locations.office: yes, named in the client supplied office list
locations.proof: Records exist in the register. Geoff, Melbourne VIC office, May 2025, $3,908,748 against a $4,172,548 appraisal, commercial deck p.7. Wendy, portfolio addition, 2024, $1,175,000, investor deck p37. The register also notes Melbourne is the largest unslotted group in the home buyer deck, so more records are available without asking the client for anything new.
locations.note: Build this one first. It is the only one of the three that can fill every slot the Brisbane template has, so it is the honest test of the template.

locations.label: Adelaide
locations.readiness: BLOCKED ON EXTRACTION, NOT ON THE CLIENT
locations.office: yes, named in the client supplied office list
locations.proof: None extracted. The investor deck holds 75 records across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide, per paper/proof-register.md, so Adelaide records exist in material the client has already supplied. They have not been pulled into the register. This is an extraction job here, not a request to the client.

locations.label: Perth
locations.readiness: BLOCKED, AND NOT BY ANYTHING THIS REPOSITORY CAN FIX
locations.office: NO. The office list supplied by the client and recorded independently in paper/commercial-copy.md and paper/investor-copy.md is Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide. Perth is not in it.
locations.proof: None, and none available. Zero Perth records across the register, and paper/commercial-copy.md records explicitly that no proof record is in Perth, Adelaide or Canberra.
locations.note: See openDecisions.perthHasNoLocalPresence. Three slots in the Brisbane template assume a local presence that does not exist in Perth.

ownLayout.decision: The location pages take their own layout. They are not derived from the buyer page the way a segment page is. What carries over is the design language and the context, not the page structure: the same Figma tokens, the same two faces, the same base components, the same voice, banned language, claim tiers and proof discipline, and the same DESIGN.md and HANDOVER.md.
ownLayout.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, from the design lead
ownLayout.consequence: assets/css/locations.css is expected to become a substantial layer rather than a thin one. Nothing is lifted out of landing.css on the assumption it will be reused: its 1330 lines are almost entirely the composition of the buyer page, and that composition does not apply here. The site header and footer are the only likely exception, and are the one open promotion, noted at the top of locations.css.
ownLayout.contrast: The segment pages are built by copying New Builds/buyer/index.html and changing only the copy and the data-segment attribute. That instruction is the one thing from the segment build that does not carry over to this family.

hubspotDelivery.decision: These pages ship in HubSpot, not on Vercel. What this repository produces is the reference implementation that gets handed to the client developer to port: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework and no React. The Vercel deploy is a preview for review and handoff, not the host.
hubspotDelivery.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, from the design lead
hubspotDelivery.consequence: The constraint is already met and must stay met. This repository has no build step, no framework and no CDN dependency, and that is now a handoff requirement rather than a preference. Nothing here may grow a compile step, a component framework or a runtime dependency, because the receiving developer works in HubSpot templates.
hubspotDelivery.watch: Two things travel badly into HubSpot and are worth designing around rather than discovering late. The asset paths are ../../ relative and become HubSpot file manager URLs, so keep every reference in one place rather than scattered inline. The two faces are self hosted from assets/fonts and need uploading to the HubSpot file manager with the same cache headers, or the largest contentful paint regresses on the H1.

seoCannibalisation.problem: DESIGN.md records that the propertybuyer.com.au homepage H1 is untouchable because it holds position one for the core commercial terms, and that this constrains what a landing page H1 may compete with.
seoCannibalisation.status: MOSTLY ANSWERED 21 Aug 2026 BY THE REFERENCE PAGE
seoCannibalisation.answer: These pages slot into an existing pattern, /location/<slug>, alongside a Brisbane page that already ranks and carries a self referencing canonical. They are siblings of a working page rather than new competitors for the homepage, so the constraint that worried me is much narrower than it looked. A city page targeting "buyers agent <city>" is not competing with the homepage for the generic term.
seoCannibalisation.remaining: Whether /location/adelaide, /location/perth and /location/melbourne already exist. If they do, this is a replacement and needs a plan for the existing URL and its rankings, which is a very different job to publishing a new page. Attempting to check this from here tripped the site bot protection, so it is unverified and the client or the developer can answer it in one look.

locationPageSegmentField.problem: Every capture point posts segment, budget_band and location. On a segment page the segment is fixed by the page and the location is typed by the visitor. A location page inverts that: the location is fixed by the page and the segment is not known. Whether the location field is prefilled and locked, prefilled and editable, or left free text with the page name only as a default, changes what arrives in HubSpot.
locationPageSegmentField.status: OPEN, DECIDE BEFORE THE FIRST BUILD
locationPageSegmentField.consequence: Getting it wrong quietly degrades lead data rather than breaking anything visible, so it will not be caught by review.

handWrittenOrGenerated.problem: Whether the location pages need a generator, given the repository deliberately has no build step and that is now a handoff requirement.
handWrittenOrGenerated.answer: No generator. One template, three pages, confirmed by the design lead. Three hand written pages is below the threshold where a generator earns its cost, and HubSpot repeats a template across rows itself, so the multiplication belongs at the destination rather than here. What is handed over is the reference pages, locations.css and the copy decks.

perthHasNoLocalPresence.problem: Perth is one of the three chosen locations, and the client has no Perth office and no Perth proof records. The office list they supplied is Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide, recorded independently in two copy decks. The proof register holds zero Perth records across 75 plus, and commercial-copy.md states outright that no record is in Perth, Adelaide or Canberra.
perthHasNoLocalPresence.consequence: Three sections of the Brisbane template assume a local presence: "Our purchases in <City>", "Your local <City> buyers' agents" with 14 named agents, and "Contact our nearest office". On a Perth page all three are empty. Filling them claims a local office and local purchases that do not exist, which is not a copy problem but a truthfulness one, and it is the exact thing DESIGN.md rule one forbids.
options: Ask the client whether a Perth office or Perth purchases exist and were simply never supplied. Cheapest answer if it is yes.

Build Perth on a variant with those three sections removed rather than emptied, and say so on the page: served from the nearest office, inspected in person. That is the claim the copy decks already make and it is true.
Drop Perth and build Adelaide and Melbourne. Two honest pages beat three where one cannot support its own structure.
perthHasNoLocalPresence.doNot: Do not fill the three slots with records from other cities, and do not name agents who are not in Perth. Do not soften this because the brief asks for three pages.

referencePageIsNotACopyModel.decision: The live Brisbane page is the structural and SEO reference for this family. It is not the design or copy model. Its anatomy, its 23 sections, its SEO gaps and its three conflicts with DESIGN.md are recorded in locations/REFERENCE.md.
referencePageIsNotACopyModel.status: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026 as to structure, OPEN as to voice
referencePageIsNotACopyModel.open: The page that performs is written in the voice the current design system was created to replace. Its meta description opens with "Discover the expertise of", and discover is on the banned CTA list. Its H1 second line is typed in capitals, which is what the Proyale capitals decision explicitly ruled out. Its authority claim is unquantified. Either this family carries an explicit voice exception, or the new pages apply the new voice and diverge from the page used as evidence. Both are defensible, guessing is not, and the choice is visible to the client.
